content.text:
I have enough to conclude. Let me verify the fee structure imposes no take-or-pay.

**Findings from investigation:**

- **§4 Fees (p0054–p0055):** License fees per Exhibit B; maintenance/support is annual but expressly conditional — "Maintenance and Support shall automatically continue during the term ... **provided that Corio continues to pay** the annual Maintenance and Support fees" — i.e., we can stop paying and simply lose the service, not incur a shortfall charge.
- **Exhibit B Revenue Sharing (p0156–p0160):** Our payment to Commerce One is a pure percentage of actual Application Management Revenue *received* from Corio Customers, accruing only "when the Corio Customer begins live operations." Purely usage/revenue-based — no floor, no guaranteed minimum.
- **Exhibit B Implementation Fees (p0161):** Time-and-materials against an agreed Statement of Work, subject to a not-to-exceed cap — ordered services only, and the cap benefits us.
- **Exhibit B/§17 (p0153, p0168):** MarketSite.net access fee is an annual fee for an ordered access service, not a volume commitment.
- **§4.4 (p0059):** The only use of "shortfall" is a reciprocal audit true-up ("the appropriate party shall promptly pay the amount of such shortfall or refund such overpayment") — a true-up mechanic, not a penalty, and it runs both ways.
- **Exhibit D (p0198, p0205):** Expressly "non-binding," and the two-customer item is only "commercially reasonable efforts."
- **p0158:** The single "minimum" reference is a metering convention (40 Authorized Software Users per Customer) inside the *waiver* of revenue share for the initial 3000 licenses — it affects how quickly the free pool is consumed, not a purchase obligation.

No take-or-pay, no volume cap on our usage, and no shortfall penalty. This meets the preferred position, so no redline.

input.quote: Corio to pay Commerce One [*] of all Application Management Revenue from Corio Customers for use of Commerce One Software or MarketSite.net Service Access subject to the following limitations.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay obligation, or volume cap on us (Corio, the licensee). Our recurring payment to Commerce One is a pure revenue share — a percentage of Application Management Revenue actually received from Corio Customers (p0157), accruing only once a Corio Customer "begins live operations" (p0160) — with no floor, guarantee, or shortfall charge. Implementation fees are time-and-materials against an agreed Statement of Work with a not-to-exceed cap (p0161), i.e., ordered services only. Annual maintenance and support is expressly conditional on our election to keep paying ("provided that Corio continues to pay the annual Maintenance and Support fees," p0055), so we can exit that spend without penalty rather than being locked into five years of fees. Exhibit D's sales and marketing items, including the two-customer target, are stated to be "non-binding" and commercially-reasonable-efforts only (p0198, p0205). This satisfies the preferred position: fees are for usage or ordered services only. Two minor points noted but not flagged: (i) the sole "minimum" reference (p0158) is a metering convention — a 40 Authorized Software User floor per Customer applied when drawing down the initial 3000 licenses granted to us — which affects how quickly that royalty-free pool is consumed rather than obliging us to buy anything; and (ii) the only "shortfall" language is the reciprocal audit adjustment in §4.4 (p0059), which is a true-up ("the appropriate party shall promptly pay the amount of such shortfall or refund such overpayment") and not a penalty. No redline required.
